talia: Heads-up: onboarding sample that wires Next+Edge -> SDK is breaking only after adapter bundling. Error in edge runtime: "TypeError: Class extends value undefined". Local node server is OK.
talia: Minimal repro + configs in the repo. Posting the snippets that reproduce it.
talia: package.json used in sample:
```
{
  "name": "rw-edge-onboard",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    "import": "./dist/sdk.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/sdk.cjs"
  }
}
```

talia: tsconfig used for sample build:
```
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "declaration": true,
    "isolatedModules": true
  }
}
```

ben: bundlers/adapters frequently transform small runtime guards (the old `if (typeof exports === 'object') ...`) into a shim that pulls in a CJS fallback. If that shim is inlined, the subclass base becomes undefined which triggers that error.
omar: do you have a snippet of the SDK export shape? that conditional glue is the usual culprit.
talia: SDK currently ships both builds and a tiny runtime switch file for local convenience:
```js
// dist/entry.js (pseudo)
if (typeof exports === 'object') module.exports = require('./sdk.cjs')
else export { default } from './sdk.mjs'
```
talia: The adapter/bundler is inlining/rewriting it and we get an undefined import for the class. Also observed "self is not defined" in another run — seems polyfills get pulled.
sophie: two separate axes: 1) runtime interop (CJS/ESM shims) which edge bundlers hate, 2) typing ergonomics where `unknown` generics leave JS sample users with no autocomplete.
ben: for runtime: safest route for edge-targeted samples is to publish/import ESM-only artifacts (no conditional runtime glue). For the package we can still ship dual builds, but the sample should explicitly import the ESM path: `exports.import` only in sample package.json or directly import `./dist/sdk.mjs`.
omar: for the typings: our SDK currently uses `request<T = unknown>(...)` and that is correct for strict TS but terrible for JS DX. Two pragmatic patterns:
1) add a JS-friendly non-generic overload that returns a loose shape, and keep the strict generic overload below it, e.g.
```ts
request(path: string, body?: any): Promise<Record<string, any>>;
request<T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T>;
```
2) add small helper entrypoints on client: `client.withType<T>()` or `client.json<T>()` that explicitly opt-in typed returns and a `client.raw()` / `client.any()` convenience for JS.
talia: we prototyped `client.withType<T>()` and `client.raw()` in the sample. `client.raw` returns Record<string, any> so JS authors get useful completion without adding generics.
ben: also try switching the sample tsconfig.moduleResolution to `node16` instead of `bundler` — bundler mode sometimes causes unexpected export rewrites in adapter toolchains. `node16` tends to be more stable for modern export maps.
sophie: i experimented enabling `esModuleInterop` to prevent the shim from being needed; runtime passed in one adapter but then several type overload tests started failing in CI (inference changed). So toggling compiler flags is noisy and affects consumers unpredictably.
omar: another build flag to check is `emitHelpers` and whether `tslib` is bundled. Sometimes downleveled helpers are duplicated and cause prototype/instanceof issues if helper duplication occurs across modules. Verify `tslib` usage and try `importHelpers: true` + external tslib to keep helpers stable.
talia: immediate plan for the sample PR: 1) switch sample to import-only ESM (remove conditional CJS guard in sample artifacts), 2) set sample tsconfig.moduleResolution to `node16`, 3) add `client.withType<T>()` and `client.raw()` helper APIs in the SDK, 4) update sample README with short JS/TS usage examples showing improved IDE inference, 5) add a post-build smoke test that imports the built ESM artifact and asserts the exported class is constructible.
ben: +1. Add an automated PR check: build sample as ESM and run it in a local adapter dev runtime (vercel dev or deno) as a lightweight smoke test. That would have caught the shim rewrite earlier.
sophie: Dev ergonomics request: include a short TypeScript example in the PR so reviewers can quickly see that `await client.withType<{embedding:number[]}>(...)` yields proper typings and that `await client.raw('/embed', {...})` yields immediate JS completion.
devx-bot: created issue #1620: "edge-sample: build ESM-only onboarding sample + adapter smoke test" with labels devex/ci priority/medium. Assigned to @talia.
talia: I'll open the PR with the changes (export tweak + helpers + post-build test) and include a tiny test that runs `node --input-type=module` to import the built `sdk.mjs` and `new Client(...)` to assert constructibility. Will ping for review when green.
ben: also include a one-line changelog: "samples: prefer ESM-only artifacts for edge adapters; add JS-friendly typing overloads and helper APIs" so external consumers know the guidance.
omar: thanks  — if the PR touches typings please add a sample in `packages/sdk/README.md` showing both JS and TS styles; it speeds review.
sophie: and log the `moduleResolution` rationale in the sample README so future authors don't accidentally revert to `bundler`.
talia: will do. ping me if anyone wants to pair on the smoke CI workflow.
